main_body: A flat grass ground patch (4x3 tiles) with scattered darker and lighter green pixel tufts repeating every 16px; no standing volume.
top_band: none - terrain tile, no standing object; uniform mid-green field with small tufts
evidence: The candidate is a seamless grass ground texture, not a standing object. Terrain is judged as a flat surface, so no top/front structure is expected. It carries no side faces and is not a front elevation. Tufts of dark and light green pixels repeat in a regular 16px pattern.

style.evidence: The grass uses about 4 greens (dark, mid-dark, base, light highlight), with sparse tufts on a large base-green field. The pattern tiles visibly every 16px: the same tuft clusters repeat in a grid, which looks mechanical next to the reference grass with its irregular clumps and variation. The base green dominates and many 5x5 zones are a single flat colour, though scattered dots break them up. Tile density is lower than the reference, which carries more distinct shades per tile. Because the repetition is obvious and the density is thinner, a careful artist would see it as less rich than Beodeul, so it fails. No outlines, as expected for ground.
